summary: CM550's user datalogger keeps its settings in the EEPROM mirror. e2m block 1282 holds four 16-byte trigger records at 0x803d64 (EEPROM 0x25a). Block 1283 (not 1282) holds five 6-byte data parameter records at 0x803da4 (EEPROM 0x29a). The machine code (16- and 6-byte strides, loop counts 4 and UDPRCU), the ROM region table (64 / 30 bytes) and the dump (UDADSZ = 94 = 64 + 30; resolved addresses = table[id] + offset) agree. The nine functions at 0x138b6-0x14292 are all the datalogger code in the dumped 256 KB ROM: trigger task, sample task, start-up, sample period, the two address resolvers, the fault-code lookup, the trigger evaluator and the 400-byte copy. Core proposal: the datalogger_trigger_t[4] / datalogger_data_parameter_t[5] instances (replacing six scalar rows) and nine standalone cm550_ function names. The block 1284 / 1285 words, the RAM working set and the event storage are secondary and separable.

structs.evidence: Type-only template (empty address). 16-byte stride: lsl.l #4 of the index at 0x13ef6 (cm550_FUN_00013ed8), moveq #16 / add.l d0,d3 (d2 in 0x13dbe) at 0x13986 / 0x13d10 / 0x13dfe / 0x13ec4; count 4: cmpi.b #4 at 0x13e06 / 0x13ecc, cmpi.w #4 at 0x13d1a, the 0-2 loop plus the separate trigger 4 (tst.b $803d95, move.w #3,-(sp)) in 0x138b6; the ROM region table (8-byte {address, length} entries at 0x8062 + 8 x e2m region) gives region 0x1F5 = {0x0100025a, 64} = 4 x 16; the dump's UDADSZ (0x803dc2) = 0x5e = 94 = 64 + 30. Every field width is from the machine code (Ghidra 12.2 CPU32 listing). e2m 1282 holds 32 records: UD0nTR.. at hex +0x10*(n-1) + BY 0 / DB 1 / FU 2 / MD 4 / NM 6 / OF 8 / TD 0xA / TY 0xE; widths 1 / 1 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 2 / 4 / 2 match. EEPROM 0x25a-0x299 equals the RAM mirror 0x803d64-0x803da3 byte for byte.

fields.name: value_length
fields.comment: +0 (e2m UD0nTRBY 'DATALOGGER TRIGGER LENGTH' 0-4): the width in bytes of the value the trigger compares: 1 = byte / 2 = word / any other value = dword (move.b (0;a0;d0.w*8);d0b at 0x13f30 then cmp.b #1 / #2 / #4); 2 in all four dump records

fields.name: disable_flag
fields.comment: +1 (UD0nTRDB 'DISABLES DATALOGGER TRIGGER INPUT'): nonzero = not evaluated; the trigger task then stores 1 (satisfied) for triggers 1-3 so the AND condition ignores them and 0 for trigger 4 (tst.b (0;a0;d3.w) at 0x1396c with a0 = 0x803d65 / tst.b $803d95 at 0x13994); 1 in all four dump records

fields.name: fault_code_flag
fields.comment: +2 (UD0nTRFU 'SET TRIGGER INPUT TO A FAULT CODE'): 1 = the trigger watches a fault code's status in the fault count table / 0 = it compares a parameter with threshold. The address is resolved only for 0 (tst.w at 0x13dd2) and the fault is looked up only for 1 (cmpi.w #1 at 0x13cf4 / 0x13e78); the evaluation takes the fault path for any nonzero value (tst.w at 0x13f00); 0 in the dump

fields.name: above_threshold_or_fault_active_flag
fields.comment: +4 (UD0nTRMD 'TRIGGER => THRESHOLD OR < THRESHOLD'): parameter trigger: nonzero = satisfied while the value is above threshold / 0 = while it is below; both strict (bls / bcc / ble / bge after cmp; tst.w at 0x13f0e). Fault trigger: nonzero = satisfied on the pass the fault status turns from inactive (0 or 2) to active (1 or 3) / 0 = on the pass it turns from active to inactive (tst.w at 0x1419c); 1 in the dump

fields.name: parameter_id_or_fault_code
fields.comment: +6 (UD0nTRNM 'NAME TABLE NAME'): with fault_code_flag 0 the parameter ID passed to cm550_lookupParameterIdAddress (move.w (0;a0;d2.w);-(sp) at 0x13de0); with 1 the fault code matched against the code word of the 125 six-byte fault definitions at 0x8067c4 (cmp.w (a2);d0w at 0x13ea0); dump 0x100c / 0x1004 / 0x1051 / 0x1047

fields.name: parameter_offset
fields.comment: +8 (UD0nTROF 'NAME TABLE OFFSET'): byte offset added zero-extended to the parameter ID's address (move.w (0;a0;d2.w);d0w / andi.l #0xffff / add.l d0;(a2) at 0x13df2-0x13dfc); dump 2 / 0x76 / 0 / 0

fields.name: threshold
fields.comment: +10 = +0xA (UD0nTRTD 'TRIGGER THRESHOLD' 0-FFFFFFFF): read as one dword (move.l (0;a0;d2.w)) and compared through its low byte for value_length 1 (andi.l #0xff - also in signed mode so a 1-byte threshold is 0-255) / its low word for 2 / the whole dword otherwise; dump 0x18fc / 0 / 0 / 0x4f

fields.name: signed_value_flag

functions.plate_comment: The datalogger's trigger task (e2m UD*; run from the scheduler slot cm550_FUN_0001b6d6 after cm550_j1939TimeoutDataClearHandler). Every pass it counts the sample period counter (0x80051e) up to the sample period (0x800353) and then raises the sample due flag (0x800354). With the datalogger enable bit clear (0x20 of feature_enable_flags_word, e2m 106B +0x26 UDEN 'BIT 5') it clears the trigger detected / AND / OR flags (0x80baca / 0x80bac6 / 0x80bac8) and the set-up flag (0x800352). Otherwise: before the set-up and with no event being logged (0x80bac4) it reloads the sample period (cm550_selectDataloggerSamplePeriod) and in automatic mode (0x803dc6 = 1) resolves the trigger parameters (cm550_resolveDataloggerTriggerAddresses) and fault codes (cm550_findDataloggerTriggerFaultIndexes); with the engine stopped (engine_state STOPPED) or an event being logged it clears the three flags; in automatic mode on a sample-due pass it evaluates triggers 1-3 of datalogger_triggers_cal (a disabled one counts as satisfied) and trigger 4 (a disabled one does not) with cm550_evaluateDataloggerTrigger into the result bytes at 0x80036a: triggers 1-3 all satisfied set the trigger detected flag and the AND flag, trigger 4 sets the trigger detected flag and the OR flag. In any other mode a rising edge of bit 6 of the byte at 0x80bcd0 (latch 0x800520) sets the trigger detected flag. No caller reads D0. (was cm550_FUN_000138b6; PR #53 round 91)

functions.plate_comment: The datalogger's sample task (run from the scheduler slot cm550_FUN_0001b6e4 after vp44_hourMeterEventLogger). While the datalogger is disabled with no trigger detected and no event being logged it zeroes the 400-byte ring buffer at 0x800374 once (flag 0x800372). Otherwise: at the set-up (0x800352 = 0, no event being logged) it sets 0x800352, resolves the data parameters (cm550_resolveDataloggerDataParameterAddresses), counts into 0x800521 the first 0x803dc8 (UDPRCU) records of datalogger_data_parameters_cal whose running byte total stays at or below 10 and points the write pointer (0x800504) at the ring. On each sample-due pass (0x800354, cleared here): a detected trigger (0x80baca) starts an event - logging active (0x80bac4 = 1), the trigger information at 0x800522 (ring offset of the write pointer / key_on_hour_meter / the low bytes of the AND and OR flags) and the post-trigger byte count (0x80051c) = 0; then value_length bytes of each counted parameter are copied from its resolved address (0x800508 + 4 x n) into the ring, wrapping at 0x800504. While logging, the 200th byte after the trigger ends the sample and sets 0x80052a; the event is then saved: the trigger information and a copy of the ring (cm550_copyDataloggerSampleBuffer) go to event 1 (0x8052ea / 0x804fca; e2m UDTRMK / UDDXTB) while UDEV01 (0x8052fa) is 0 and to event 2 (0x8052f2 / 0x80515a) otherwise, UDEV01 / UDEV02 (0x8052fc) are set and logging stops - an event holds the 200 bytes before and the 200 after its trigger. functions.plate_comment: Returns 1 when datalogger trigger trigger_index (0-3) of datalogger_triggers_cal is satisfied, else 0. Parameter trigger (fault_code_flag 0): it reads value_length bytes (1 = byte / 2 = word / any other value = dword) at the trigger's resolved address (dword 0x800356 + 4 x index) and compares them with threshold (its low byte / low word / the whole dword), unsigned or signed by signed_value_flag, strictly above (above_threshold_or_fault_active_flag nonzero) or below (0). Fault trigger (fault_code_flag nonzero): the fault count table status byte (0x805a24 + 10 x the fault index at 0x800366 + index) against the status it saw last (0x80036e + index): a nonzero flag fires when the status went from inactive (0 / 2) to active (1 / 3), 0 when it went from active to inactive; it then saves the status. Status bit 0 = active: cm550_FUN_00014872 stores 3 when a fault turns active and 2 when it turns inactive, cm550_diagnosticCodeRegistrar stores 0 / 1 when it takes the fault's snapshot slot and cm550_diagnosticTableEntryClear stores 0.
